top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks are a mature, well-defined invention: magic-wavelength trapping removes the lattice light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated on an ultranarrow transition, giving about 1e-18 fractional uncertainty, reproduced with Sr, Yb and Hg in several laboratories and already used for tests of constants and relativistic geodesy. The two-person allocation to Katori (invention and magic-wavelength concept) and Ye (realisation and accuracy record) is clean and within the three-laureate limit, and the citation stays within what the record supports. No award is clearly inferior given this maturity.
recusal_note: No specific conflict apparent from profile beyond general field proximity as an atomic physicist and laser spectroscopist; no documented connection to Katori or Ye.
